correctness.rationale: The two adjacency relations are explicit on Z4×Z4 and all 65,536 vertex masks per graph are exhaustively tested. Independent degree and forbidden-subgraph face predicates agree on every mask. All strongly regular parameters, face vectors, maximal-face counts, matching pairs and critical multisets are asserted by a standalone checker. The common fixed vertex order creates 639 and 543 matched pairs on the new complexes, leaving one critical vertex and 57 or 105 critical three-cells. A complete topological sort on 4,960 and 4,224 oriented face incidences verifies the acyclic matching condition. Forman’s discrete Morse theorem then gives a CW complex with one zero-cell and only three-cells; all three-cell attaching maps land in a point, so the full integral homotopy types are precisely the claimed wedges. The checker reproduced VERIFY_OK from actual package files. The r=1 comparison is separately reproduced but is only historical context.

originality.rationale: The published ordinary-independence comparison for the same exceptional strongly regular pair computes Ind_1, not Ind_2; no logical implication supplies the new homotopy types or degree-three sphere counts. The closely related full-text primary sources classify complete multipartite, whiskered, path, cycle, tree, or chordal graph classes; the two six-regular nonchordal graphs fall outside their stated hypotheses. Actual semantic research-database and public literature searches for the exact objects, alternative dissociation terminology, degree-one induced-subgraph constraints, and stronger graph-family statements did not reveal a covering theorem. This is a best-knowledge assessment with explicitly acknowledged risks.
residual_risks: The exact earlier ordinary-comparison record was retrievable by scientific search summary but its complete GitHub text was unavailable; a stronger result hidden in that work is not independently excluded by full-text inspection.
An unindexed thesis, unpublished computation, or another source could contain equivalent 57 and 105 sphere-wedge calculations.
The original 1959 graph-classification primary full text was not accessible; it is background rather than an apparent source of higher-complex homotopy calculations.

value.rationale: The pair of exceptional strongly regular (16,6,2,2) graphs is a canonical example of spectral twins. Their ordinary independence homotopy types were already known to have 23 versus 15 two-spheres. The first higher-independence step reverses their sphere-count order to 57 versus 105 three-spheres. The new result provides two complete nonpure integral homotopy classifications and an interpretable comparison of a natural graph-complex invariant, not just another face enumeration or graph-name substitution. The exact dimensions and multiplicities furnish a benchmark for homotopy sensitivity beyond strongly regular parameters and are not consequences of prior r=1 results.
